items.stem: For producing one million identical simple plastic clips, why is additive manufacturing usually not the best choice?

options.text: Additive is slow per part and has high unit cost at high volumes, where moulding or machining scale better
options.rationale: Correct: additive excels at complexity and low volume, not high-volume identical simple parts.

options.text: Additive cannot print plastic at all
options.rationale: Additive commonly prints plastics; volume economics are the issue.

options.text: Additive always produces stronger parts than any other method
options.rationale: Strength varies; this is not why additive loses at high volume.
Additive needs a digital model; this is unrelated to the volume question.

items.explanation: Correct: additive excels at complexity and low volume, not high-volume identical simple parts.

items.stem: Which TWO are genuine strengths of additive manufacturing? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Producing complex geometries that are hard or impossible to machine
options.rationale: Correct: additive builds internal channels and lattices machining cannot.

options.text: Economically making low-volume or customised parts
options.rationale: Correct: additive suits prototypes and customisation without tooling.

options.text: Always being cheaper than every other process at any volume
options.rationale: Additive is not always cheapest, especially at high volume.

options.text: Eliminating any need for design knowledge
options.rationale: Good results still require design-for-additive knowledge.

items.explanation: Correct: additive builds internal channels and lattices machining cannot.

items.stem: Why does part orientation matter when planning a 3D print?

options.text: Orientation affects strength, surface finish and how much support material is needed
options.rationale: Correct: orientation changes layer direction, supports and quality of the result.

options.text: Orientation has no effect on a printed part
options.rationale: Orientation significantly affects strength and finish.

options.text: Orientation only changes the part's colour
options.rationale: Colour is a material choice, not an orientation effect.

options.text: Orientation determines the CAD software used
options.rationale: Orientation is a print-planning decision, not a software selector.

items.explanation: Correct: orientation changes layer direction, supports and quality of the result.
